authority: This file is the only place the free/pro split and the free caps are defined. src/utils/feature-gate.js loads it at runtime. config.json and feature-registry.js point here and carry no numbers.

notSold.auto_tagging: No implementation exists in src/. Nothing in the codebase produces a tag suggestion. Verified 2026-08-09 by grep across src/ for autoTag, auto_tag, suggestTags. Not gated, not advertised, not sold until it is built.

splitRationale.offline_reading: Free and uncapped. The live listing title is 'ReadLater Pro, Save and Read Offline', so this is the printed promise. The save handler in src/background/service-worker.js blanks article.content when the gate denies, so any cap destroys the article body at capture time rather than locking a view. A cap here is data loss, not a wedge.
splitRationale.bulk_export: Free. Pocket import is free and the stated audience is people escaping a shutdown. Charging to get data back out of an escape hatch is the lock-in this product sells against.
splitRationale.reading_stats: Free. Low willingness to pay, and it is the surface that produces the honest 'you finished N articles' number that earns the upgrade ask.
splitRationale.full_text_search: Pro, metered not locked. The only Pro candidate that is actually implemented: src/utils/db-manager.js filters on options.fullTextSearch across article.textContent. It is a true multiplier over the free title and tag search, non-destructive when unavailable, and it scales with library size so only heavy users reach the cap.
splitRationale.listen_aloud: Pro, metered not locked. Free users get 3 articles a day read aloud, counted once per article per local day when playback starts (reopening or resuming an article already counted today is free; the count resets at the user's local midnight). Uses the browser's own voices, so nothing is lost when the cap is reached: the article is still there to read.
splitRationale.markdown_export: Pro with one free try (firstTouchGrace). A formatting convenience for note apps. Getting data out stays free: CSV in Pocket's format, bookmarks HTML and the full JSON backup (with tags and highlights) are free, so bulk_export's no-lock-in promise holds.

firstTouchGraceNote: Applies only to a Pro feature with NO numeric free cap: it grants exactly one use so the wall never lands on the first touch. full_text_search is not listed because a cap of 20 a day already gives the user twenty wins before the wall, which satisfies the same timing rule.
